To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
increasing context heterogeneity reduces attention deployment towards an item embedded in the context and that this is reflected in occiptal theta and alpha band activity.

the occipital alpha band activity of a source cluster was reduced in the heterogeneous compared to homogeneous context, and that the theta band activity of a different cluster was increased in the heterogeneous compared homogeneous context.

(i) the amplitude of the N170 and N2pc decreased monotonically with increasing context heterogenity, (ii) the amplitude of N2 exhibited a non-monotonic U-shaped function of heterogeneity, (iii) occipital theta activity was modulated by heterogeneity level, (iv) the occipital theta band was modulated by the presence of a target item, and (v) occipital alpha band activity varied with heterogeneity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question how the human brain processes heterogeneous visual scenes, and how the degree of heterogeneity influences visual attention.
the question how the brain processes heterogeneous visual contexts.
the question of whether and how the degree of heterogeneity of a background affects the deployment of visual attention.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
context heterogeneity affects visual attention in a way that is reflected in occiptal alpha and theta band brain activity.
increasing heterogeneity reduces attention deployment and that this effect is reflected in occiptal brain activity.
increasing heterogeneity in visual search is accompanied by reduced attention deployment and less efficient target processing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the occipital cortex is involved in the differential deployment of visual attention to heterogeneous versus homogeneous contexts.
increasing heterogeneity in the context reduces attention deployment, which is reflected in occpital alpha and theta activity.
increasing context heterogeneity reduces visual attention deployment, which is reflected in occipto-parietal ERP components and brain sources.
The main takeaway from our work is that
context heterogeneity is an important factor in attentional selection.
context heterogeneity can be induced by varying whole field heterogeneity.

the degree of heterogeneity in a visual search task is not only a matter of the degree to which the background is segmented into perceptual groups, but also a matter of how the background variability is distributed over the whole field.
